stem: What is the most common underlying cause of hypertension in children?
explanation: Renal disorders are the most common underlying cause of hypertension in children, particularly renal parenchymal and renovascular disease.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because renal parenchymal and renovascular diseases are the most frequent underlying causes of hypertension in the paediatric population.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because essential hypertension is less common in children than secondary hypertension, particularly renal causes.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because endocrine causes can produce hypertension but are less common than renal disorders in children.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because psychological stress may raise blood pressure transiently but is not the most common underlying cause of paediatric hypertension.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because coarctation of the aorta can cause hypertension but is less common than renal disorders overall.
